requirement: The `habeas` skill MUST tell agents that a new project with little code starts with `habeas-requirements`, not `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, even though most of its code has no references.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The bundled `habeas` skill must tell agents that a new project with little code starts with `habeas-requirements`, not `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`, even though most of its code has no references.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_starts_a_new_project_with_the_requirements_skill]` covers it. It takes step 1 of the `habeas` skill's Workflow section through `step("habeas", 1)`. That helper uses `workflow_steps`, which parses the bundled skill's numbered steps and panics if the step or the workflow is missing. The test then calls `assert_text`, which asserts that the step text contains each listed phrase and fails with a message if one is missing. The two phrases are:
- The routing row, "Adopting Habeas in an existing codebase, or most of the code has no references | habeas-bootstrap-requirements". This pins the existing-codebase case to the bootstrap skill, so the new-project guidance has something to contrast with.
- The sentence "A new project with little code starts with habeas-requirements, not habeas-bootstrap-requirements, even though most of its code has no references". This matches the full obligation: the new-project case, the `habeas-requirements` skill, the not-bootstrap contrast, and the "most code has no references" caveat.

The assertions check the required content directly, and the test carries the `{test}` reference to the subject. The requirement names no other modes or boundaries. No gaps found.
